blocks.text: *How your abilities work, and where they come from.*

In Unwritten, **your equipped weapon carries its own kit of active skills.** Equip a sword and your hotbar fills with that sword's abilities; swap to a bow and the bar becomes the bow's kit. There are no classes in Unwritten — your weapon is what defines your abilities, and changing weapons is how you change your loadout.
Every weapon rolls its own kit

Each weapon *type* has its own **pool of skills** — **3 ultimates** plus a set of normal skills (how many depends on the weapon; the pool is only as large as the weapon's identity naturally supports). No single weapon gives you all of them; a weapon holds up to **1 ultimate + 3 normals**, and what it drops with depends on its **rarity** — higher rarity means more skills already filled in and a better chance of carrying an ultimate. (A common weapon might drop with a single skill; a legendary can arrive nearly complete.) You can then **craft** the rest — see *Crafting & Recycling*.

**Your ultimate points at your build.** Each weapon's three ultimates each steer toward a different playstyle — and which Ring stats to invest in — so the ultimate you roll is a hint at how to build that weapon.

So two of the same weapon can play very differently, and chasing the weapon (and the ultimate) *you* want is part of the hunt. Every skill in a weapon's pool reinforces that weapon's identity — so whatever you roll, it still plays like that weapon.
Skills don't level — your Ring powers them

A skill's raw strength doesn't come from ranking the skill up. Instead, **your Ring stats scale it** (see *Stats & the Ring*). The same skill is stronger in the hands of someone who invested the right stats. This is what keeps roles honest: a heal only pays off if you invested MP; a damage skill only hits hard if you invested Attack or Magic Attack.
What a skill is made of

items: **Its numbers** — how much damage, how many hits, how long it lasts, its mana cost, cooldown, cast time, range, and area.
**Its effects** — what it actually *does*.

blocks.text: Most skills are **active**: they take a hotbar slot, and you press them. They cost mana and use the cooldown, cast time, range, and area above.
Some are **passive**. A passive takes **no hotbar slot and is never pressed** — it waits for a specific moment in the fight and fires on its own. The moment it waits for is part of the skill:

items: **After you finish casting a particular skill** — uninterrupted. This is how one skill rides another: Lock Blades off Lunge.
**When a basic attack of yours lands.**
**When you kill something.**
**When you drop to low health.**
**When you're hit.**
**When you successfully parry.** Opening rides this one.

blocks.text: A passive **fires as a full skill** — the same visuals and the same effects an active would play. Only the trigger is different. It aims itself, too: a skill that needs a target lands on whatever set it off, and a skill that targets you always lands on you.
Skills are built from a catalog of effects. The common ones:

items: **Damage** — direct harm (physical, magic, or forced-crit).
**Heal / Regen / Shield** — restore health now, heal over time, or raise an absorbing barrier.
**Guard** — cut incoming damage for a while.
**Buff** — raise your damage, attack speed, or cast speed.
**Status ailments** — Burn, Poison, and Bleed (damage over time), plus Slow, Stun, Freeze, Silence, and Blind.
**Haste** — speed yourself up (or slow enemies down).
**Vulnerability** — mark a monster to take extra damage.
**Taunt** — force monsters to attack you.
**Knockback / Pull** — shove enemies away or drag them in.
**Mana Leech / Reflect** — briefly turn damage you deal into mana, or bounce damage back at attackers.
**Cleanse** — strip debuffs off yourself.
**Execute** — bonus damage that grows huge against low-health enemies.
**Dash / Teleport** — close distance in a rush, or blink to a target spot.

blocks.text: **Ultimate skills** are a special tier that charge up during combat and cost that charge to unleash — every weapon's pool holds **3** of them, and a weapon can carry **one** (higher-rarity drops are far more likely to come with it).

text: *Status: the skill framework above is in place. Exact numbers, cooldowns, and each weapon's skill pool are still being tuned and drafted.*
